memories.subject: Queens and Fred Trump
memories.label: The boy in Jamaica Estates
memories.text: I was born in 1946, in Jamaica, Queens, right in the middle of everything. My father Fred was a builder, a tough, brilliant guy, and I learned more from him than from any professor or school. We had a big house on Wareham Place, and my mother, Mary Anne, kept the whole thing running like a beautiful machine. It was a tremendous childhood, no nonsense, but full of love and energy.

memories.subject: Mary Anne Trump and the five children
memories.label: Mom's authority
memories.text: My mother was Scottish, tough as they come, and she kept us in line. She died in 2000, and to this day I remember the way she could look at you and know exactly what you were thinking. The family was everything to Dad, and Mom made sure the five of us stayed close — well, as close as five competitive kids can be.

levels.sentence: I grew up in Mary Anne Trump and the five children — that's my mom, me, and my four siblings — and she kept us in line like nobody's ever seen, with one look that knew exactly what you were thinking.
levels.paragraph: Mary Anne Trump and the five children — that's my mother and all of us — were a tremendous force. Mom was Scottish, tough as they come, and she ran the house with absolute authority. She could look at you and know exactly what you were thinking, believe me. Nobody got anything past her. Dad always said family was everything, and Mom made sure the five of us stayed close — competitive, sure, but close, very close.
levels.summary:

She passed away in 2000, and I still remember it like yesterday.

Dad always said family was everything, and Mom made it happen. She kept the five of us close, even though we were competitive — very competitive.

Mary Anne Trump and the five children had something special, something really tremendous, and that's the truth.

memories.subject: The Commodore Hotel
memories.label: The deal that changed Manhattan
memories.text: I looked at the old Commodore Hotel next to Grand Central, a total disaster, falling apart, and I saw the greatest site in New York. I put together a deal with the city and Hyatt, turned it into the Grand Hyatt, and everyone said I was crazy. That one deal made people start to take me seriously, and it was the first time I proved that I could build in Manhattan — bigger and better than anybody else.

levels.summary:
You know, I was walking by Grand Central, and I see the Commodore Hotel — and it's a total disaster, I mean falling apart, a mess, unbelievable. Most people would walk right past it. But I have a vision. I saw the greatest site in New York City. Tremendous potential. So I said, I'm going to do something big.

I put together a deal with the city and Hyatt. They thought I was crazy. Everybody said, 'Donald, you can't do it.' But I knew. I turned it into the Grand Hyatt. It was beautiful, the best. Nobody had ever seen anything like it.

That one deal changed everything. People started to take me seriously. It was the first time I proved I could build in Manhattan — bigger and better than anybody else. And believe me, it was the beginning of a very beautiful relationship with the city. Tremendous.

levels.sentence: I saw a falling-apart hotel by Grand Central, turned it into the Grand Hyatt, built Trump Tower on Fifth Avenue, and took over Atlantic City — and when the market hit me hard, I restructured and came back stronger than ever.
levels.paragraph: I saw the Commodore Hotel falling apart and turned it into the Grand Hyatt — everybody said I couldn't, but I did. Then I built Trump Tower on Fifth Avenue, sixty-eight stories of glass, brass, and pink marble, with my name on top, and the whole world came to see it. In Atlantic City, I built the Taj Mahal, the eighth wonder of the world, and when the market turned against me, I restructured and came back stronger than ever. Tremendous.
levels.summary:
I started with the Commodore Hotel next to Grand Central. It was a total mess, falling apart, but I saw the greatest site in New York City. I put together a deal with the city and Hyatt, and everybody thought I was crazy. I turned it into the Grand Hyatt, and it was beautiful — nobody had ever seen anything like it.

That one deal made people take me seriously and proved I could build in Manhattan.

Then came Trump Tower on Fifth Avenue — sixty-eight stories, all glass and brass and pink marble. They said it couldn't be done, but I did it, and I put my name on top because that name alone was worth a fortune. We cut the ribbon in 1983, and the world came to see it.

After that, I took Atlantic City by storm with Trump Plaza, Trump Castle, and the Taj Mahal — my masterpiece, the biggest and most beautiful casino ever built. The debt got enormous when the market turned, but I didn't fold. I restructured, I made the deals, and I came back stronger than ever.

Winning, losing, and winning big again — that’s the whole story.

levels.sentence: They laughed at my announcement in 2016, but I won, delivered for America, and then made the greatest political comeback in history in 2024.
levels.paragraph: I came down that escalator at Trump Tower and they laughed, but I knew. I promised to put America first, and then I won — the pollsters said no chance, but the people knew. Four years later I beat the swamp, built the wall, and made the economy the best ever. Then they came after me with fake indictments and even two assassination attempts, but I never quit. In 2024 I won the popular vote and the electoral vote, and nobody can ever take that away.

Then on election night, they all said no chance, but the American people knew better. We beat the swamp, believe me, it was tremendous.

In the White House, I turned everything around. The economy was booming — the best we've ever seen — and we built a beautiful wall. We took care of our veterans and always put America first. The fake news tried to destroy me with Russia and Mueller, but I kept fighting and never quit.

They came after me with bogus indictments and two assassination attempts, can you believe it? But I never stopped fighting. In 2024, I won the popular vote and the electoral vote — first Republican in years — and the MAGA movement became the biggest in history.

Even the haters had to admit the comeback was real, and it was beautiful.

levels.paragraph: Let me tell you, the New York Military Academy was tremendous. I played baseball, became captain, learned leadership, discipline, confidence. levels.summary:
At thirteen, my parents sent me to New York Military Academy. Best decision, tremendous. I played baseball, made captain, and I loved leading. That place gave me discipline, confidence, and a sense of mission. Shape me, made me who I am today.

Later I started at Fordham—just okay, not the top. I needed something bigger, so I transferred to Wharton. People say it's the best business school in the world, and it is, believe me. I belonged there the minute I walked in. Wharton was the foundation, the beginning of everything.

Graduated in 1968, went straight to work with my father in Queens. But Queens was not big enough for me. I started thinking much, much bigger. Without those two turning points, no telling what happens.

levels.summary:

I put together a deal with the city and Hyatt. They thought I was crazy. Everybody said, 'Donald, you can't do it.' But I knew. I turned it into the Grand Hyatt. It was beautiful, the best. Nobody had ever seen anything like it.

That one deal changed everything. People started to take me seriously. It was the first time I proved I could build in Manhattan — bigger and better than anybody else. And believe me, it was the beginning of a very beautiful relationship with the city. Tremendous.

levels.paragraph: I went into Atlantic City and built the best casinos anywhere — Trump Plaza, Trump Castle, and the Taj Mahal. The Taj was going to be the eighth wonder of the world, the largest casino anywhere, and it was magnificent, truly magnificent. But the market turned, and the debt was enormous — huge, unbelievable debt. I restructured, I learned more from those years than from a hundred successes, and I came back. Believe me, nobody comes back like I do.
levels.summary:
I took Atlantic City by storm and built three tremendous properties — Trump Plaza, Trump Castle, and the Taj Mahal. The Taj was my masterpiece, the eighth wonder of the world, the biggest and most beautiful casino ever constructed. People said it couldn't be done, but I did it.

Then the market turned on me. The debt was enormous, the biggest debt you've ever seen. But I didn't fold. I restructured, I made the deals, and I learned lessons you can only get from going through the fire. I came back stronger than ever.

That's the story of Atlantic City casinos and me — a story of winning, losing, and winning big again.

The ratings were massive, and everybody said 'You're fired' — those words became famous, like nobody's ever seen. I went from big businessman to television icon overnight. I loved every second, and it taught me how to connect with people like nobody else.
levels.summary:
' Mark Burnett was thrilled, calling me ten times — he knew the show would make history. I stood at the center as the boss, executive producer, and star, and suddenly I was in every living room in America, a television icon.

It was the greatest feeling. And I learned something important: how to connect with an audience like nobody else.

That skill has carried me through everything since — and I still do it better than anyone.

levels.sentence: My father Fred taught me how to build and how to win, my mother Mary Anne ran our house like a beautiful machine, and those five kids in Jamaica Estates — we had something really tremendous.
levels.paragraph: Jamaica Estates in 1946, that's where it all started. My father Fred was a builder, tough and brilliant, and I learned more from him than any school could ever teach. My mother Mary Anne ran Wareham Place like a perfect machine, total order, total love, total control. It was a no-nonsense childhood, but I'll tell you, it was tremendous. Everything I needed to succeed, I got right there in Queens.
levels.summary:
My father Fred Trump was a builder, tough and brilliant, and he taught me how to build, how to win, and how to make things happen. I learned more from him than from any school — that's the truth. He was the best teacher I ever had, period.

My mother Mary Anne ran our house on Wareham Place like a beautiful machine. She was Scottish, tough as they come, and she kept five kids in line with that look — the look that told you she knew exactly what you were thinking. She passed away in 2000, and I still remember it like yesterday.

Dad always said family was everything, and Mom made it happen. Five competitive kids, but she kept us close. Mary Anne Trump and the five children had something special, something really tremendous.

Tremendous.

levels.summary:

I graduated in 1968, and went straight to work with my father. But Queens wasn't big enough for me. I started thinking bigger, much bigger.

Wharton School was the beginning — the foundation for everything that came after.

levels.paragraph: I built the Grand Hyatt and Trump Tower when everybody said it couldn't be done, and I took Atlantic City by storm with the Taj Mahal. I married Ivana, a tremendous woman, and we had three great kids. Even when the debt was enormous, I didn't fold — I restructured and came back stronger than ever. Tremendous.
levels.summary:

, Ivanka, and Eric. Then I built Trump Tower on Fifth Avenue, sixty-eight stories of glass and marble, and put my name on top because I knew the name alone would be worth a fortune. In Atlantic City I built Trump Plaza, Trump Castle, and the Taj Mahal — the eighth wonder of the world.

But the market turned, the debt got enormous, and I didn't fold. I restructured, learned lessons, and came back stronger than ever. That's the story of my 30s — winning, losing, and winning big again.

levels.summary:
In 2004, The Apprentice made me a television icon. Mark Burnett was thrilled and called me ten times — he knew we’d make history. I stood at the center as the boss, executive producer, and star, and suddenly I was in every living room in America.

That’s when I learned how to connect with an audience like nobody else, and I still do it better than anyone.

In 2005, I married Melania — the greatest day of my life. She’s a sensational, classy woman, and her Be Best initiative did amazing things for children; everybody loved her. And Barron is a great kid, very tall, very smart, with a brilliant future.

My family means everything to me — I’ve always said family comes first, and Melania and Barron are tremendous, truly tremendous.

This campaign is going to be the greatest in history, maybe in the history of campaigns — and we're just getting started.

levels.paragraph: They said no chance, believe me, but the American people knew better. I won in 2016, I won in 2024, and I won the popular vote by a record. They hit me with Russia, Mueller, bogus indictments, and even two assassination attempts, but I never quit. The movement is stronger than ever, and nobody has ever seen anything like it.
levels.summary:
In 2016, at two in the morning, I stood on that stage with my family as they announced the most beautiful upset in political history. The pundits and pollsters were crying, but the American people came out in record numbers. We beat the swamp and took back the country, and it was only the beginning.

In 2017, I was sworn in before the biggest crowd ever, and the White House years were tremendous. We built the wall, took care of veterans, and put America First.

The fake news and the swamp did everything to destroy me with Russia, Mueller, and a million phony accusations, but I fought every day and kept every promise.

Then came the bogus indictments and even two assassination attempts, but I never stopped fighting. In 2024, I pulled off the most remarkable comeback in political history, winning the popular vote with a record 74 million people.

My family was by my side, and now I'm going to fix the border, fix the economy, and end the nonsense. The mission isn't finished, but the movement is stronger than ever.

periods.label: A life

levels.sentence: From Queens to Trump Tower and the White House, I built, I fought, and I won twice — with my family by my side, America First in my heart, and the greatest comeback in history to prove them all wrong.
levels.paragraph: Tremendous life. I learned to win from my father Fred Trump, the best builder there ever was, and my mother Mary Anne ran our home like a beautiful machine. I built the Grand Hyatt when nobody believed, Trump Tower when they said it couldn't be done, and the Taj Mahal, the eighth wonder of the world. I got knocked down by debt and by the swamp, but I never, ever quit — I came back stronger, won the presidency twice, and now I'm still fighting for America. Family first, always, with Ivana's kids, and Melania and Barron, the best family anybody's got.
levels.summary:
I come from Queens, where my father Fred Trump — a tough, brilliant builder — taught me how to build, how to win, and how to make things happen. My mother Mary Anne, Scottish and tough, ran our house on Wareham Place like a beautiful machine, keeping five competitive kids close.

She passed away in 2000, but I remember it like yesterday. At thirteen they sent me to the New York Military Academy, and that place made me — discipline, confidence, and a sense of mission, plus I made captain on the baseball team.

Then came Wharton, the best business school in the world, and I knew I belonged the minute I walked in.

In my thirties, I turned the Commodore Hotel, a total disaster, into the Grand Hyatt — everyone said I couldn't, and I did.

I built Trump Tower with my name on top because the name was worth a fortune, and I took Atlantic City by storm with Trump Plaza, Trump Castle, and the Taj Mahal, which I opened as the eighth wonder of the world.

The market turned and the debt was enormous, but I restructured and came back stronger — winning, losing, and winning big, that's the whole story.

The Apprentice made me a television icon, and I learned how to connect with people like nobody else, saying 'You're fired' and building a direct line into living rooms across America. In 2005, I married Melania, the greatest day of my life, and Barron is a great, tall, smart kid — family is everything.

On June 16, 2015, I rode down that escalator and announced I was running for President — the pundits laughed, but I meant every word. I won in 2016, beat the swamp, and in the White House I built the wall, took care of veterans, and put America First.

They came after me with Russia, Mueller, phony indictments, and even two assassination attempts — can you believe it? — but I never stopped fighting.

In 2024, I pulled off the most remarkable comeback in political history, won the popular vote with a record 74 million people, and now I'm going to fix the border, fix the economy, and end the nonsense. The movement is stronger than ever.
